New raw `raw/stripe-payments-sunbit-accept-a-payment-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-sunbit-accept-payment-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-sunbit-accept-payment.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sunbit/accept-a-payment`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sunbit/accept-a-payment establishes six navigation choices in new raw lines 9-20: Checkout, Checkout Sessions API and Payment Intents API with Elements, Direct API, iOS and Android. It supplies no fresh prerequisites or payment states. The 2026-05-06 full capture, old raw lines 8-1839, describes a single-use US/USD installment method. Checkout is payment-mode only, uses a single currency across line items, and lists a $60.00 to $19,999.99 USD compatibility range. The merchant server creates a Checkout Session or PaymentIntent as appropriate and hands the client the corresponding scoped secret where the integration uses one. The customer authorizes with Sunbit and returns, with success or failure notification. The optional manual redirect uses a PaymentIntent in requires_action with next_action.redirect_to_url, and the success event is distinct from browser return. source-stripe-sunbit-accept-payment.md compresses this evidence, omits the mobile variants, and overstates universal return_url, Session-creation enforcement, and manual-capture certainty.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/sunbit/accept-a-payment the 2026-11-07 index in new raw lines 9-20 replaces the displayed full bodies from 2026-05-06 in old raw lines 8-1839 with selectors. It provides no substantive flow or support change and no removal evidence. Preserve the May Checkout eligibility and amount bounds as compatibility, the different Checkout success_url, Checkout Session return URL examples and PaymentIntent confirmation return_url, the sandbox/live distinction and separate native callbacks. Qualify the unconditional no-manual-capture statement in source-stripe-sunbit-accept-payment.md: the May Sunbit profile and November BNPL API matrix mark it unsupported, while the November Sunbit profile marks it supported. Preserve the May raw as full evidence, add November as six-route navigation, and keep the root-to-Stripe index, existing Stripe BNPL concept, and source links reciprocal.
